prompt: Build a Fraction class whose constructor reduces the fraction to lowest terms using gcd and keeps the denominator positive, with a plus method that returns a new simplified Fraction and a toString of the form "num/den".
explanation: Doing the simplification once in the constructor means every Fraction object is always in lowest terms, so plus can simply build the raw sum and let the constructor clean it up. The classic Euclidean algorithm computes the gcd, and flipping both signs when the denominator is negative keeps a single canonical form (-1/2 rather than 1/-2). Returning a new Fraction from plus keeps the class side-effect free.
hints: In the constructor, first check if den < 0 and if so negate both num and den.
The Euclidean algorithm: while b != 0, replace (a, b) with (b, a % b); a is then the gcd. Use Math.abs(num) so negatives do not break it.
For plus, compute (a*d + c*b) and (b*d), then return new Fraction(...) -- the constructor will simplify it for you.
